Fire damages historic stage. Flames tore through the backstage of Cripple Creek's 1896 opera house overnight, though the auditorium survived.
My first job was ushering at the Apollo, and I watched Les Mis about two hundred times.
We went to the Minack, cut right into a cliff in Cornwall, and the sea was the backdrop to the whole play.
Which London playhouse is a reconstruction of the one Shakespeare's company built in 1599?
Which ancient Greek theatre at Epidaurus is famous for acoustics so good a coin drop can be heard from the top row?
Hi Ella, we saw Hamilton at the Victoria Palace! The chandelier, the gilt boxes, I was gawping before it even started.
Hey Max, the little fringe venue above the Hen and Chickens is doing an improv night Thursday. Only 60 seats.
Ford's Theatre in Washington, where President Lincoln was shot in 1865, reopened as a working playhouse in 1968.
This painted backdrop was used at the Bolshoi in Moscow for the 1877 premiere of Swan Lake.
Tonight on Curtain Call we're backstage at the Abbey in Dublin, where the cast are warming up in the green room.
Big news for the West End, folks: the Phoenix is going dark for refurbishment, and ticket holders are being moved to the Cambridge.

topic:Amphibian.text: There's a fire salamander on the path!! Black and yellow, so cute
Froglets in the pond! Common toads I think, hundreds of them
Chester Zoo announces the hatching of thirty critically endangered Kihansi spray toads, a species extinct in the wild.
The Axolotl Rescue Project has released 200 captive-bred axolotls into restored canals at Xochimilco.
Q: How does the wood frog survive winter? A: It freezes solid. The heart stops, and in spring it just thaws and hops off.
Q: Why is the golden poison frog so toxic? A: Its skin holds batrachotoxin from the insects it eats; captive ones lose it.
Keeping a horned frog? Use damp coconut fibre, keep it around 26 C, and feed it gut-loaded crickets twice a week.
Helping toads cross the road in spring? Carry them in a bucket in the direction they were heading and wear a hi-vis vest.
Rare salamander rediscovered in Guatemala. Jackson's climbing salamander, unseen for 42 years, was found by a guard in a cloud-forest reserve.
Fungus kills off harlequin frogs. Researchers say chytrid has wiped out several Panamanian populations of the bright-coloured toad.
I picked up a cane toad as a kid in Queensland and my dad screamed, because they ooze poison from the glands behind their heads.
We were at a creek in North Carolina and found a hellbender, a two-foot salamander that looked like a wrinkled old wallet.
Which Mexican salamander keeps its feathery gills for its whole life?
Which giant salamander from China can grow up to 1.8 metres long?
Hi Jess, the great crested newts are back in our garden pond! Orange bellies and little dragon crests. Have to tell the council survey.
Ollie, the coqui frogs in Puerto Rico sing all night, 'ko-KEE, ko-KEE'. I loved it, Dan did not.
The Goliath frog of Cameroon can weigh more than three kilograms and builds its own nest pools along river banks.
Caecilians are legless, burrowing relatives of frogs; some mothers feed their young on a layer of their own skin.
Tonight on Nature Hour: listener Pat says a bullfrog in her pond sounds like a cow. Pat, that's how it got its name!
Caller from Devon reports a natterjack toad chorus on the dunes at night, louder than the waves. What a treat, Sue.

topic:Arachnid.text: HUGE huntsman on the ceiling, I am not sleeping in here tonight
Found a tick on the dog after the hike, got it out with tweezers
The Natural History Museum announces the discovery of a new jumping spider species in Peru, named Maratus elisae after a young volunteer.
Wildlife officials confirm the noble false widow is now established across southern Ireland and urge calm.
Q: How strong is Darwin's bark spider silk? A: Tougher than Kevlar by weight. It spans webs 25 metres across rivers in Madagascar.
Q: Why do scorpions glow under UV light? A: Compounds in their outer shell fluoresce blue-green, though nobody's sure why.
To catch a house spider, put a glass over it, slide a postcard underneath, and release it outside.
Checking for ticks after a walk? Look behind knees, ears and the waistband, and remove them close to the skin.
Funnel-web found in Sydney pool. A male Atrax robustus survived 30 hours underwater before being caught for the antivenom program.
Peacock spider goes viral. A tiny Australian jumper with a fan-like rainbow abdomen has millions of views after a researcher filmed its dance.
I was camping in Arizona and shook out my boot, and a bark scorpion fell out. I check every boot now, forever.
My son keeps a Chilean rose tarantula called Doris, and when she molts, there are two of her in the tank.
Which venomous spider has a red hourglass marking on its abdomen?
Which tiny mite lives in the hair follicles of most human faces?
Hi Abby, a garden orb weaver built a web across our porch every night this week. I've named her Charlotte.
Hey Ravi, saw harvestmen everywhere in the woods. Turns out they're not spiders at all, just eight-legged cousins.
The Goliath birdeater of South America has a leg span of up to 30 cm and flicks irritating hairs when threatened.
This amber holds a 99-million-year-old Chimerarachne, an extinct arachnid with a tail and spinnerets.
Gardener's Question Time: Jim, those red specks on your tomatoes are red spider mites, so mist them and bring in predatory mites.
Listener calls in about a wolf spider carrying hundreds of babies on her back. Mum of the year, Dave!

topic:Bird.text: A robin keeps landing on my shovel while I dig lol
Red kite over the M40 again, they're everywhere now
The RSPB announces that white-tailed eagles have bred on the Isle of Wight for the first time in 240 years.
The Kakapo Recovery Programme reports a record 55 chicks this season for the flightless New Zealand parrot.
Q: How far does the bar-tailed godwit fly? A: Over 11,000 km nonstop from Alaska to New Zealand, eleven days without landing.
Q: Do crows really recognize faces? A: Yes. American crows remember people who've bothered them and scold them for years.
Want goldfinches at your feeder? Put out nyjer seed in a tube feeder with small ports.
To tell a chiffchaff from a willow warbler, listen: the chiffchaff sings its name, 'chiff-chaff-chiff'.
Hoopoe spotted in Norfolk. A pink, crested African visitor delighted birdwatchers on a village lawn near Cley.
Ivory-billed woodpecker still unconfirmed. Scientists released new drone footage from Louisiana but critics remain unconvinced.
I was on Skomer and a puffin walked right past my foot with a beak full of sand eels.
My grandma had a budgie called Pip that could say 'Who's a pretty boy' and whistle the Archers theme.
Which flightless bird is the largest living bird in the world?
Which bird, extinct since about 1681, lived only on Mauritius?
Hi Sara, the peregrines on the cathedral spire have three chicks this year. The webcam is live, have a look!
Hey Tim, saw a kingfisher on the canal this morning. Just a blue flash, but definitely one.
The passenger pigeon once numbered in the billions; the last one, Martha, died at Cincinnati Zoo in 1914.
The male bowerbird of Australia decorates his bower with blue objects, from berries to bottle caps, to attract a mate.
Birdsong hour: listeners, that bubbling call is a curlew, and its numbers have halved in Britain since the 1990s.
Caller says a woodpecker's drumming on his gutter at 5 am. Gary, he's not after bugs, he's advertising!

topic:Crustacean.text: Caught 6 blue crabs off the dock, steaming them tonight!
Found a hermit crab in a cone shell at the beach
The Marine Institute announces that a new species of deep-sea amphipod, Eurythenes plasticus, was found in the Mariana Trench with plastic in its gut.
Maine officials report the lobster landings dipped slightly last year, with the American lobster still the state's biggest catch.
Q: How hard does a mantis shrimp punch? A: Its club accelerates like a bullet and can crack aquarium glass.
Q: Why is Antarctic krill so important? A: Whales, penguins and seals all depend on it; its biomass is one of the largest of any animal.
To cook langoustines, boil for two minutes in salted water, then shock in ice to keep the meat sweet.
Keeping cherry shrimp? Use a planted tank and avoid copper-based treatments.
Coconut crab census on Christmas Island. Rangers counted 2,000 of the giant land crabs, which can crack coconuts with their claws.
Red crab migration closes roads. Millions of Christmas Island crabs are marching to the sea to spawn.
I went tidepooling in Oregon and a goose barnacle colony looked like little dinosaur feet.
My grandad caught a lobster in Cornwall that was bright blue, and he put it back because it was so rare.
Which large Japanese crab has the longest leg span of any arthropod?
Which crustaceans glue themselves head-first to rocks and kick food into their mouths?
Hi Leo, crawfish boil Saturday! Ten pounds of mudbugs, corn and potatoes.
Hey Ann, did you know woodlice are crustaceans? Our garden's full of them.
The Tasmanian giant freshwater crayfish can weigh over 5 kg, and is threatened by overfishing.
Copepods like Calanus finmarchicus are tiny but feed herring, cod and whales across the North Atlantic.
Seafood report: Dungeness season opens Friday, and the boats are loading pots in Half Moon Bay.
Caller says her son's sea monkeys hatched. They're brine shrimp, Liz, and congratulations!

topic:Fish.text: Caught a 5 lb largemouth bass off the dock at the lake!!
Snorkel was amazing, a clownfish kept darting in and out of its anemone
The Monterey Bay Aquarium announces that an ocean sunfish has joined its Open Sea exhibit for the first time in a decade.
Fisheries managers report a record sockeye salmon return to Bristol Bay this summer, with more than 70 million fish counted.
Q: How old can a Greenland shark get? A: Possibly over 400 years. It grows less than a centimetre a year in that cold water.
Q: Why does the deep-sea anglerfish carry a light? A: Glowing bacteria in the lure on its head attract prey in total darkness.
Keeping a betta? Give it a heated tank of at least 20 litres and never house two males together.
Cooking mackerel? Grill it skin-side down until crisp and serve with something sharp, like gooseberry or rhubarb.
Coelacanth filmed off Indonesia. Divers recorded the 'living fossil' at 150 metres inside a volcanic cave near Sulawesi.
Tuna fetches 1.3 million dollars. A 212-kilogram bluefin set a record at Tokyo's first auction of the year.
I was fly fishing for brown trout in Montana and a bald eagle swooped down and took one right off my line.
My dad kept koi in the backyard pond, and one named Big Orange lived for over thirty years.
Which lobe-finned fish, thought extinct for 66 million years, was found off South Africa in 1938?
Which flat, round ocean fish is the heaviest bony fish in the world?
Hi Alice, I swam next to a whale shark at Ningaloo! It was the size of a bus and totally calm.
Hey Paul, a pike in the gravel pit took my lure and bit straight through the line. Teeth like a saw.
The Atlantic cod built whole economies around the North Atlantic; the Newfoundland fishery collapsed in 1992 after decades of overfishing.
The mudskipper spends much of its life out of water, skipping across mangrove mud on its pectoral fins.
And here comes the salmon run at Brooks Falls, a sockeye leaps right into the bear's mouth!
Fishing show: caller just landed a 40-pound striped bass off Montauk Point on a live eel. Nice job, Mike!

topic:Insect.text: Monarchs all over the milkweed in the garden today!
A stag beetle just flew into the kitchen, it's the size of my thumb
The Xerces Society announces that the endangered rusty patched bumble bee has been recorded at twelve new sites across Minnesota.
Melbourne Zoo reports the hatching of more than 1,000 eggs of the Lord Howe Island stick insect, once thought extinct.
Q: How far do monarch butterflies migrate? A: Up to 4,800 km, from Canada to the oyamel fir forests of central Mexico.
Q: Why do fireflies blink? A: Each species has its own flash code, and males and females use it to find each other.
To bring ladybirds into the garden, plant dill and fennel and leave a few aphids alone for them to eat.
Keeping Indian stick insects? Feed them bramble or privet leaves and mist the tank lightly every other day.
Giant hornet nest destroyed in Washington. Officials vacuumed out the first nest of Asian giant hornets found in the United States.
Cicada brood emerges. Billions of 17-year periodical cicadas are surfacing across northern Illinois this month.
I was in Michoacan and walked into a forest where monarchs covered every trunk, and when the sun hit them, the trees took off.
As a kid I kept a praying mantis named Bob, until Bob ate her boyfriend and we had to rethink the name.
Which beetle did the ancient Egyptians revere as a symbol of the rising sun?
Which social insect performs a 'waggle dance' to tell hive mates where flowers are?
Hi Clare, saw a hummingbird hawk-moth on the lavender today. Hovering, long tongue, I honestly thought it was a bird.
Hey Sam, the dragonflies at the pond were huge today, emperors I think, bright blue and patrolling like helicopters.
The Atlas moth of Southeast Asia has a wingspan of up to 25 cm, and adults have no mouths, living only a week or two.
Leafcutter ants do not eat leaves; they chew them into pulp to farm a fungus that feeds the whole colony.
Listener asks why the crickets are louder tonight. Count chirps for 14 seconds, add 40, and you've got the temperature in Fahrenheit!
Caller from Kent says honeybees swarmed on his car wing mirror. Don't panic, Ken, a local beekeeper will collect them for free.

topic:Mollusca.text: Found a giant African land snail on the patio, it's the size of my hand!!
Octopus at the aquarium just unscrewed a jar lid in front of us
The Monterey Bay Aquarium announces that its giant Pacific octopus, Kiki, will move to a larger habitat with new enrichment puzzles.
Marine biologists confirm the first successful captive breeding of the chambered nautilus at a public aquarium.
Q: How smart is the common octopus? A: Very. They solve mazes, open jars, and some escape tanks at night to raid neighbouring ones.
Q: Why is the cone snail dangerous? A: It fires a venomous harpoon tooth fast enough to paralyse a fish, and some species can kill a person.
Cooking mussels? Discard any that stay open when tapped, steam for four minutes with wine and garlic, then toss the ones that don't open.
To keep slugs off hostas, sink a shallow dish of beer into the soil overnight.
Giant squid filmed in Gulf of Mexico. Researchers using a light lure captured the first footage of Architeuthis in US waters.
Zebra mussels found in new lake. Officials say the invasive shellfish were likely carried on a boat trailer.
I was diving in Cebu and a cuttlefish changed colour five times while I watched, like a living screen.
My grandma gathered periwinkles on the rocks in Donegal and we'd eat them with a pin.
Which mollusc has three hearts and blue blood?
Which invertebrate has the largest eyes of any animal, as big as dinner plates?
Hi Fran, the nudibranchs in the tide pools at Point Lobos were unreal, purple and orange with frilly gills.
Hey Joe, guess what, our oysters from the farm in Wellfleet were the best I've ever had.
Giant clams of the Indo-Pacific can live over 100 years and weigh more than 200 kilograms.
Murex sea snails gave the Phoenicians Tyrian purple, a dye so costly that it became the colour of emperors.
Fishing report: squid are biting under the lights at the pier, folks with jigs are filling buckets.
Caller from Brighton says she found an octopus in a rock pool. Lucky you, Jen, they're shy!

topic:Reptile.text: Gecko on the bathroom wall chirping at me lol
There's a sea turtle nest roped off on our beach
The Galapagos Conservancy announces that 136 young giant tortoises have been released on Espanola Island.
Zoo Atlanta confirms the hatching of two endangered Komodo dragons from eggs laid without a male.
Q: Do chameleons change colour to blend in? A: Mostly no, it's for signalling mood and temperature.
Q: How does the leatherback turtle survive cold seas? A: Its huge body holds heat, and it keeps warm enough to dive below 1,000 metres.
Keeping a leopard gecko? Give it a warm hide at 32 C, a cool side, and dust its crickets with calcium.
To move a snapping turtle off the road, nudge it from behind with a broom, never pick it up by the tail.
Burmese python found with deer inside. Florida researchers removed a 5-metre snake from the Everglades.
Gharial hatchlings spotted in Nepal. Conservationists say the narrow-snouted crocodilian is breeding again in the Babai river.
I picked up a slowworm as a kid and it dropped its tail, still wriggling. Freaked me out.
We were in Kakadu and a saltwater croc slid off the bank right next to the boat.
Which Indonesian lizard is the largest living lizard?
Which hooded snake is the longest venomous snake in the world?
Hi Kate, we saw marine iguanas on Fernandina sneezing salt, honestly adorable.
Hey Ben, my neighbour's tortoise, Gerald, turned 70 this week.
The tuatara of New Zealand is the last surviving member of an order of reptiles that thrived alongside the early dinosaurs.
The Gila monster of the Sonoran Desert is venomous, and its saliva inspired a diabetes drug.
Listener says a grass snake swam across his pond. Don't worry, Jack, it's harmless.
Caller from Florida says an alligator is in her pool. Call the trapper, Diane!

topic:Fungus.text: Found a fly agaric in the birch wood! Red with white spots, like a fairy-tale toadstool
Chicken of the woods on the old oak by the gate, huge orange shelves
Kew Gardens announces the naming of a new species of truffle-like fungus from Western Australia, Hydnangium kewensis, found by a citizen scientist.
The Forest Service confirms that a single honey fungus in Oregon's Malheur forest covers nearly 10 square kilometres, among the largest organisms on earth.
Q: How does Ophiocordyceps control ants? A: It grows through the ant's body and makes it climb and bite a leaf before the fruiting stalk bursts out.
Q: Why are Perigord truffles so expensive? A: They grow underground around oak roots and can only be found by trained dogs or pigs.
Foraging for chanterelles? Check for false gills that run down the stem like wrinkles, and never eat anything you can't identify with certainty.
To clean morels, slice them in half lengthwise and swish them in cold water to flush out grit and insects.
Death cap spreads to new region. Mycologists warn that the deadly Amanita phalloides is now fruiting under oaks in British Columbia parks.
Mould behind penicillin returns to lab. Scientists revived spores of Fleming's original Penicillium culture for genetic sequencing.
We were hiking in Oregon and found these little bird's nest fungi, tiny cups with 'eggs' inside, and my kid thought fairies lived there.
My Italian nonno would vanish at dawn every October to his secret porcini spot and never tell anyone where it was.
Which mould, noticed by Alexander Fleming in 1928, led to the first antibiotic?
Which mushroom, scarlet with white warts, is famous from fairy tales and video games?
Hi Jen, we did a fungi walk in Epping Forest and saw a stinkhorn. Smelled exactly like it sounds.
Hey Mo, the oyster mushroom kit on my counter just exploded overnight. Stir-fry Friday?
Lion's mane fungus grows as a cascade of white icicle-like spines on hardwood trees and is edible when young.
Saccharomyces cerevisiae, baker's yeast, is a single-celled fungus that has raised bread and fermented beer for thousands of years.
Garden hour: Pete, that white web in your lawn is fairy-ring fungus, and the ring grows outward every year.
Caller found ghost fungus glowing green on a log in the Blue Mountains. Bioluminescence, Kath, it's beautiful!

topic:Grape.text: Picking Pinot Noir this weekend at the vineyard, need extra hands!
Tried an Assyrtiko in Santorini today, super crisp, buying a case
Wines of Portugal announces a campaign to promote Touriga Nacional, the country's flagship red variety, in American restaurants.
The Okanagan wine association reports that Riesling plantings have grown by 20 percent, driven by demand for dry styles.
Q: Why is Cabernet Sauvignon so widely planted? A: It's hardy, thick-skinned, and makes long-lived reds almost anywhere warm enough.
Q: What made Carmenere vanish from Bordeaux? A: Phylloxera wiped it out; it survived in Chile, mislabelled as Merlot for a century.
Pairing Gewurztraminer? Its lychee and rose notes go brilliantly with spicy Thai or Indian food.
Growing Concord vines at home? Plant in full sun, train on a trellis, and prune hard in late winter.
Ancient variety rediscovered in Sicily. Researchers identified a lost grape, Orisi, in an abandoned vineyard near Trapani.
Heatwave hits Malbec harvest. Mendoza growers are picking two weeks early to keep acidity in the grapes.
We were in Hungary and the winemaker poured Furmint from a dusty bottle and told us it's the soul of Tokaji.
My dad grew Muscadine on the back fence in Georgia, and we'd pop the thick skins and spit out the seeds.
Which grape variety is the main red grape of Burgundy?
Which white grape is the backbone of New Zealand's Marlborough region?
Hi Tess, found a gorgeous Nebbiolo from Barolo for your birthday, tar and roses on the nose.
Hey Dom, the Zinfandel at that Sonoma winery was jammy and 15 percent. Careful, ha.
Chardonnay, a cross between Pinot Noir and the obscure Gouais Blanc, became the most famous white variety of Burgundy.
Sultana, also called Thompson Seedless, is the most widely grown table and raisin grape.
Wine hour: tonight we taste Sangiovese, the heart of Chianti, cherry, leather and high acidity.
Caller says her Tempranillo smells of vanilla. That's the American oak, Rosa.

topic:RaceHorse.text: Frankel's first foal running at Newmarket today, putting a tenner on it
Did you see Rich Strike win at 80-1?? I screamed
Coolmore announces that Derby winner Auguste Rodin will stand at stud in 2026, at a fee to be confirmed.
The Melbourne Racing Club confirms that champion mare Winx will be honoured with a statue at Caulfield.
Q: How fast was Secretariat in the Belmont? A: 2:24 for a mile and a half, winning by 31 lengths. Nobody's touched it.
Q: Why was Seabiscuit so popular? A: An undersized, knobbly-kneed horse beating War Admiral during the Depression; people saw themselves in him.
Picking a winner? Look at the horse's form, the going, and how it's moving in the paddock before the race.
At the Grand National, back a horse with experience over big fences, and keep an eye on the weights.
Red Rum memorial unveiled at Aintree. The three-time Grand National winner is buried by the winning post.
Enable retired after record third Arc bid. The mare won eleven Group 1 races.
I was at Cheltenham when Kauto Star won his second Gold Cup, and the roar went right through you.
My grandad was a stable lad and he'd tell us about Arkle eating Guinness with his oats.
Which horse won the Triple Crown in 1973 by 31 lengths in the Belmont?
Which Australian mare won 33 consecutive races?
Hi Lou, I backed Tiger Roll at the National and he won again!
Hey Gus, did you hear Desert Crown's foal fetched 2 million at Tattersalls?
Eclipse, foaled in 1764, was unbeaten in 18 races; the saying 'Eclipse first, the rest nowhere' came from him.
Phar Lap, New Zealand-bred, won the 1930 Melbourne Cup; his heart is in Canberra.
And they're round Tattenham Corner in the Derby, City of Troy still has ground to make up, but here he comes down the outside!
Into the final furlong, Galopin des Champs clear, Cheltenham on its feet!

topic:Conifer.text: Standing under General Sherman right now, my neck hurts from looking up
The larches on the hill have gone gold, so pretty this week
Save the Redwoods League announces the purchase of 200 acres of old-growth coast redwood near Big Sur, including a tree estimated at 1,200 years old.
The National Park Service confirms that a Great Basin bristlecone pine in California's White Mountains is more than 4,800 years old.
Q: How did the monkey puzzle tree get its name? A: A Victorian visitor joked it would puzzle a monkey to climb, because the branches are armoured in sharp scales.
Q: How was the Wollemi pine found? A: It was known only from fossils until 1994, when a ranger stumbled on a grove in a canyon near Sydney.
To keep a Nordmann fir from dropping needles, saw a centimetre off the trunk and keep the stand topped up with water.
Growing a Japanese black pine bonsai? Pinch back the new candles in spring and keep it in full sun.
Tallest tree's location kept secret. Hyperion, a 116-metre redwood, is now off-limits after hikers trampled the ground around it.
Ancient yew may top 5,000 years. Experts say the churchyard yew at Defynnog in Wales could be the oldest living tree in Britain.
I hugged a Douglas fir on Vancouver Island that took four of us, holding hands, to reach around.
My grandfather planted a row of Leyland cypress in 1985, and now it blocks the sun from three gardens.
Which conifer species, native to coastal California, is the tallest tree in the world?
Which needle-bearing tree turns gold and drops its needles every autumn, unlike most evergreens?
Hi Zoe, the old Scots pines in Abernethy forest are stunning, flaky orange bark and twisted crowns. Crossbills everywhere too.
Hey Ian, the Christmas spruce in Trafalgar Square came from Oslo again this year, a gift every year since 1947.
The dawn redwood, Metasequoia glyptostroboides, was known only from fossils until living trees were found in a Chinese village in 1944.
Cedar of Lebanon timber, prized for its fragrance and resistance to rot, was shipped across the ancient world for temples and palaces.
Garden hour now: Barbara, your Colorado blue spruce is browning from the inside, which is usually needle cast fungus, so thin it for airflow.
Caller says his juniper hedge went brown after the heatwave. Peter, cut back to green wood only, junipers won't regrow from bare stems.

topic:CultivatedVariety.text: Honeycrisp are on sale at the farm stand, grab two bags!
Planted three 'Brandywine' tomatoes and one 'Sungold' in the raised bed today
The University of Minnesota announces the release of 'Triumph', a new hardy apple variety that keeps for five months in cold storage.
David Austin Roses introduces 'Emily Bronte', a soft pink English rose with a strong tea scent, launching at the Chelsea Flower Show.
Q: Why are all Cavendish bananas the same? A: They're clones, grown from cuttings, so a single disease like Panama TR4 can threaten the whole crop.
Q: How did the 'Peace' rose get its name? A: It was bred in France before the war and named in 1945, the week Berlin fell.
Growing 'Bloody Butcher' corn? Plant in blocks, not rows, so the tassels pollinate properly.
For 'Bramley's Seedling' apples, store them in a cool shed wrapped in newspaper; they'll cook up fluffy until spring.
Original Bramley tree dies at 200. The Nottinghamshire tree that gave Britain its favourite cooking apple has finally succumbed to honey fungus.
Gardeners' pick of the year. The 'Purple Haze' carrot, a deep violet outside and orange core, won the All-America Selections award.
My grandma grew 'Kentucky Wonder' pole beans every summer, the vines went right over the shed roof.
We went to Keukenhof and saw 'Queen of Night', the almost black tulip, and my daughter wanted a hundred.
Which apple cultivar, discovered in Australia in 1868, is named after the woman who found it?
Which popular navel orange was introduced from Brazil to California in the 1870s?
Hi Mel, I grafted a 'Cox's Orange Pippin' onto our old rootstock and it actually took!
Hey Ray, the 'Hass' avocado tree in my yard finally fruited. All Hass trees descend from one tree in La Habra.
Gros Michel bananas dominated world trade until the 1950s, when Panama disease forced the switch to Cavendish.
The Bartlett pear, known as 'Williams' in Europe, was grown in England in the 1700s and taken to America.
Garden hour: Joan, that 'Moonlight' runner bean is self-pollinating, so it'll set pods even without bees.
Caller asks about 'Chandler' strawberries. Big, sweet and productive, Rob, just pick before the rain.

topic:Fern.text: Fiddleheads are up along the creek, ostrich fern season!
My Boston fern finally has new fronds, after almost dying last month
The Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh announces that the Killarney fern, one of Europe's rarest, has been successfully propagated from spores.
Conservationists confirm the rediscovery of a tiny Hymenophyllum in Hawaii's Waianae Mountains, its translucent fronds just one cell thick, unseen for 50 years.
Q: How do ferns reproduce without seeds? A: Spores under the fronds grow into tiny heart-shaped plants, which make sperm and eggs.
Q: Why did Victorians obsess over ferns? A: 'Pteridomania': collectors stripped hillsides of hart's-tongue and maidenhair for parlour cases.
To keep a maidenhair happy, never let its soil dry out and keep it out of direct sun.
When foraging fiddleheads, pick only Matteuccia struthiopteris, with a smooth stalk and a deep U-shaped groove, and cook them thoroughly; bracken is not safe to eat.
Bracken invasion on moors. Rangers say the fast-spreading fern is choking heather across the Peak District.
Climbing invader spreads in Florida. Old World Lygodium microphyllum is smothering cypress trees in the Everglades under curtains of lacy fronds.
In New Zealand we walked through a gully full of ponga, and the silvery undersides of the fronds glowed under the canopy.
My aunt had a staghorn mounted on a board on her porch, antler-shaped fronds and all, and it grew bigger than her dog.
Which fern's silver leaf underside is a national symbol of New Zealand?
Which tiny floating fern, Azolla, hosts a nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterium?
Hi Rosa, I found an Osmunda regalis by the bog at the bottom of the hill, nearly two metres tall with rusty spore spikes on top!
Hey Nick, the hart's-tongue growing out of the old churchyard wall is still glossy green in January. Tough little thing.
Tree ferns like Dicksonia antarctica grow only a few centimetres a year, so a 4-metre trunk may be 200 years old.
The resurrection polypody, Pleopeltis polypodioides, grows on live oak branches, curling up brown in drought and turning green within hours of rain.
Garden hour: Lynne, your Japanese painted fern scorched because it's in afternoon sun; move it to dappled shade and keep the soil moist.
Caller says her Asplenium nidus has brown tips. That's low humidity, Grace, so put it in the bathroom or on a pebble tray.

topic:GreenAlga.text: The pond's gone green again, it's all that filamentous algae, ugh
Sea lettuce all over the rocks at low tide, so slippery
The Algae Biomass Organization announces a pilot farm that will grow Chlorella vulgaris for protein-rich animal feed.
Scientists at Kyoto University report sequencing the genome of the marimo ball alga from Lake Akan.
Q: How does Chlamydomonas swim? A: It has two whip-like flagella and an eyespot that steers it toward light.
Q: Why is Volvox so interesting? A: It's a hollow ball of thousands of cells, a glimpse of how multicellular life began.
Got marimo moss balls? Change their water every two weeks and roll them gently to keep them round.
To clear Spirogyra from a garden pond, twirl the slimy strands onto a stick and float a bag of barley straw to slow regrowth.
Killer alga spreads in Mediterranean. Caulerpa taxifolia, a bright green invasive seaweed, is now covering seagrass beds off Spain.
Green tide smothers Brittany beaches. Officials closed several bays as rotting sea lettuce released hydrogen sulphide gas.
In high school biology I saw Volvox spinning under the microscope, little green planets with babies inside.
We went to Lake Akan in Japan to see marimo, velvety green balls rolling on the lake floor.
Which green seaweed, nicknamed the 'killer alga', escaped from an aquarium in Monaco in 1984?
Which green alga lives in the fur of sloths?
Hi Ella, the snow on Mount Rainier was pink! It's a green alga, Chlamydomonas nivalis, with red pigments.
Hey Max, my aquarium rocks are covered in green hair algae again, Cladophora tufts everywhere. Getting Amano shrimp to eat it.
Acetabularia, the mermaid's wineglass, is a single cell up to 10 cm tall, used in classic experiments on the nucleus.
Ulva, known as sea lettuce, grows on rocky shores worldwide; dried and powdered as aonori, it is sprinkled on okonomiyaki in Japan.
Garden radio: Tom, that green blanket weed on your pond is Cladophora, not toxic, just rake it out and leave it on the bank overnight so critters crawl back.
Caller says her bird bath turns green every week. That's Chlorella-type algae, Brenda, so scrub it and change the water every couple of days.

topic:Moss.text: Roof is covered in those green cushions again, Tortula all over the north tiles, need to call someone
Found a carpet of glittering wood moss in the forest, so soft
Scottish Natural Heritage announces a project to restore 2,000 hectares of Sphagnum bog in the Flow Country, locking away carbon for centuries.
The British Bryological Society reports the rediscovery of the rare hair moss Polytrichum swartzii on a Welsh mountaintop.
Q: Why is Sphagnum so good at holding water? A: Half its cells are empty, porous chambers that soak up twenty times their weight.
Q: How does the desert moss Syntrichia caninervis survive? A: It dries completely and revives within seconds of rain.
To start a moss garden, use acidic soil, shade, and press in fragments of local cushion moss, misting daily.
Want living wall art? Blend a handful of Bryum with buttermilk and paint it onto a shaded brick wall.
Glowing moss draws crowds in Japan. Hikari-goke, the luminous Schistostega pennata, shines gold-green in a cave in Hokkaido.
Peat moss ban for gardeners. The UK will end retail sales of peat-based compost to protect Sphagnum bogs.
I lay down on a hummock of haircap in a Norwegian forest, and honestly it was softer than my hotel mattress.

Which moss, also called peat moss, forms bogs that store huge amounts of carbon?
Which cave-dwelling moss, nicknamed 'goblin's gold', seems to glow because its cells focus dim light like tiny lenses?
Hi Kira, the Hoh rainforest was dripping with Isothecium, whole maple limbs wrapped in green curtains. Felt like walking inside a sponge.
Hey Dan, in Ireland we saw a hummock of red Sphagnum as bright as paint.
In World War I, dried Sphagnum moss was used as wound dressing because it absorbed blood and resisted infection.
Buxbaumia aphylla, the bug-on-a-stick, has almost no visible leaves; what you see is a shiny brown spore capsule perched on a short stalk.
